insights.title: Highest comeback momentum

insights.title: Longest post-comeback retention
insights.text: Rainbow — Lim Young Woong stayed on the Top 50 for 296 calendar days (292 observed snapshots) after its 31 Jul 2024 re-entry.

insights.title: Fastest rank recovery
insights.text: With you — Jimin & HA SUNG WOON recovered 22 rank places (50 -> 28) in 1 day(s): 22.0 places/day.

insights.title: Strongest artist comeback behaviour
insights.text: Among artists with at least 3 re-entries, Jimin has the highest fandom intensity proxy (100/100, 35 re-entries across 24 songs, mean momentum 57.2).

insights.title: Single vs album
insights.text: Re-entries of album-track songs have a higher median momentum (49.8) than single songs (48.6); n=230 vs 162. The difference is not statistically distinguishable (Mann-Whitney p=0.279, effect size negligible). Association only.

insights.title: Explicit vs clean
insights.text: Re-entries of Explicit songs have a higher median momentum (51.5) than Clean songs (48.8); n=17 vs 375. The difference is not statistically distinguishable (Mann-Whitney p=0.807, effect size negligible). Association only.

insights.title: Re-entry rate: single vs album
insights.text: single songs: 35% had a re-entry (0.24 per 100 exposure days, n=304); album songs: 25% (0.22 per 100 exposure days, n=232); Fisher exact p=0.018. The share-of-songs rate does not adjust for how long songs stay on the chart (median appearances: single 17, album 6), so read the exposure-adjusted figure as the fairer comparison. Association only.

insights.title: Re-entry rate: explicit vs clean
insights.text: Explicit songs: 11% had a re-entry (0.05 per 100 exposure days, n=98); Clean songs: 35% (0.27 per 100 exposure days, n=439); Fisher exact p<0.001. The share-of-songs rate does not adjust for how long songs stay on the chart (median appearances: Explicit 3, Clean 17), so read the exposure-adjusted figure as the fairer comparison. Association only.

insights.title: Duration relationship
insights.text: Longer songs are associated with higher momentum (Spearman rho=0.05, p=0.296, n=392); the association is weak.

insights.title: Unusual momentum patterns
insights.text: No re-entry exceeds the IQR outlier fence (108.9); momentum is evenly spread. 14% of re-entries followed an absence of 30+ observed snapshots, and 3% were still on chart when data ended.

recommendation_notes: Album tracks show a higher median re-entry momentum (49.8, n=162) than singles (48.6, n=230); difference not statistically distinguishable (p=0.279, effect negligible). Investigate non-single promotional opportunities - directional only.
limitations: The data are observed daily Top-50 playlist snapshots, i.e. observed chart behaviour only.
The Fandom Intensity Proxy is a behavioural proxy; playlist position is not a direct measure of total fandom size.
Correlation does not establish causation; content findings are associations.
Missing calendar dates can affect time-based interpretation; they are never treated as exits or as presence.
Popularity scores are platform/API-derived and may be updated with a lag or use opaque methodology.
External causes (releases, tours, TV, promotions, social trends) are not observed in this dataset.
A Top-50 cut-off censors information: songs just below rank 50 are invisible, and exits near rank 50 can be rank noise (hence the adjustable minimum-absence threshold).
Songs on the chart at the start (left-censored) or still on it at the end (right-censored) have incomplete histories; retention for the latter is a lower bound.
Momentum scores are relative (percentile-based within re-entries); 50 means a typical re-entry, not an absolute level.
Events from the same song/artist are not independent; statistical p-values are indicative.
One date (01-03-2025) held two stacked snapshots; the retained one was chosen by similarity to neighbouring days and the two were near-equal, so a few presence flags that day are uncertain.
The re-entry forecast is experimental/descriptive and should not be read as a dependable prediction.

reentry_forecast_model_EXPERIMENTAL.reason: Discriminates well (AUC 0.903) but does not improve on a trivial recency-only baseline (AUC 0.904); the signal is almost entirely 'recently exited songs return sooner'. Treat as a descriptive risk ranking, not a validated forecast.
